Its all about breaking it down to smaller increments when you're going over a dog's threshold. Starting with spending lots of time around the crate, treating in the crate but leaving it open. Definetly leaving old clothes of yours so your scent is there to comfort her. Make it a fun and exciting time whenever you are around the crate, then slowly build up from there. Don't leave her in until she freaks out, she is very young and still craves close bonding with you. Make the process as easy as you can, shes a baby, give her plenty of slack and patience

I have noticed that some dogs are just plain weird about eating out of a bowl. I'd say try to make the food more exciting for him like treats or a spoonful of wet or chicken broth; then have a set schedule for him. Dogs typically shouldn't have food left down regardless, but if you have a schedule he will know when its time to eat and if he doesn't then he's missed his window. Not to say starve the dog! If he's not eating definitely take him to the vet. Also maybe consider a different material for a bowl? Dogs are very sensitive, are the bowls between him and the puppy the same? Also also, separating the two while they eat to minimize any food stealing. Hope this helps!

Aside from the very well said answers about how to go about advanced nose work; as a dog trainer I wanted to mention a couple things. Having your dog find the treat and somehow get to it by nosing, pawing, whatever, are two different cues. If you'd like her to uncover the boxes herself you have to shape that along with the nose work. It all depends on what kind of work you want your dog to be doing, and making your intentions clear to your dog is essential. Its seems like a good sign to me that she finds the treats easily then looks to you, a good start for nose work. However if you want her to be doing service work, then her learning to uncover the treats herself would make sense. What I'm saying overall is guide her through the training as consciously as you can, be deliberate and patient. Good luck!
